answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can submit one bid per day. Agents named lotus, willow, and walnut each face the same rule: extra identities require extra deposits, so splitting one balance across aliases creates no free bidding capacity. An attacker seeking 1,000 daily bids must immobilize 100,000 tokens, bearing financing costs and token price risk throughout the lockup.
